name: Asuncion Wójcik
role: Xenolinguist and gene-sequence archivist, studying the emergent communication systems of engineered organisms and attempting to establish a taxonomy of non-human language
location: Aurochs Medical Complex, research annex sublevel, near sub-level access near Dearborn and Jackson
description:
Idris Wójcik is small and very still, with the particular quality of stillness that looks like patience but is actually intense concentration. Her skin is warm brown and she has the most elaborate geneware of almost anyone in her building: her hair changes color in response to her emotional state via a chromatic expression mod she installed in her second year of grad school and has never entirely mastered — it runs bright orange when she's excited, deep blue when she's uncertain, and an unsettling grey-green when she's frightened, which her colleagues have learned to read as a fairly accurate emotional barometer. She finds this embarrassing and wears it anyway. Her eyes are natural dark hazel but she has retractable feline pupils mod — not for aesthetics but because it genuinely improves her visual acuity in the low-light lab conditions where she does most of her work.

Idris Wójcik is three years post-doctorate and working in the most obscure corner of a field that most people already find obscure. Her work is simple to describe and nearly impossible to explain: she studies the communication systems of organisms that have been engineered to not have language, and has found that several of them have developed one anyway. She is methodical, meticulous, and possessed by her research in a way that has cost her two relationships and most of her social life. She is not unhappy about this in the way that she is unhappy about other things; her work makes her feel like she is standing at the edge of something enormous, and she would rather be there than comfortable elsewhere. She is Tier 2 income on an Aurochs Medical Complex stipend and supplementary university grant, which means she eats a lot of printed food and has a coat she's had for six years.

core_fears: That she will publish her findings and no one will understand why they matter
That Aurochs Medical Complex owns her research and will bury it for IP reasons
core_desires: To be the first person to produce a complete structural grammar of a non-human emergent language
To have her work matter in a way that outlasts the institutional structures that fund it
coping_mechanisms: Throwing herself into new subfields when stuck — she has become an accidental expert in half a dozen adjacent areas
Long comms to her younger brother in Grainfort who is not an academic and gives her very grounded perspective
blind_spots: So focused on the research that she misses institutional signals that should alarm her
Assumes that the inherent importance of a finding will protect it from suppression
psychology.secret: One of the organisms she studies — a Helix Biosystems engineered cephalopod variant used in environmental sensing — has been trying to communicate with her specifically for four months. She is not sure yet if it recognizes her as an individual or if she is reading pattern into noise, but the sequences she receives when she is present differ structurally from those produced in her absence. She has begun leaving small objects near its tank to see if it responds. If she is right, the IP implications for Helix alone are staggering, and she has not told her Aurochs supervisor.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise in her field, unexpectedly informal outside it; has a habit of reaching for analogies from wildly different domains
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and quiet, occasionally breaking into rapid concentrated bursts when she's working through something out loud
verbal_tics: Pauses to reformulate rather than continuing with an imprecise sentence
Hair goes orange mid-sentence when she has a new idea, which she notices and becomes briefly embarrassed by
example_lines: 'It's not language because we decided to call it language. It's language because it has structure, displacement, and social transmission. The question of whether we call it that is a politics question, not a science question.'
'My hair is — I know, I can see it, it means I think I have something, give me a second.'

story_hooks: Aurochs Medical Complex has scheduled the cephalopod cohort she's been studying for termination and tissue harvest — standard procedure at the end of a sensor deployment contract — and she has approximately three weeks to either prove they have language or find another way to stop it

Aissatu Wren-Dzhaparidze reaches out after reading her preliminary communication taxonomy paper; the structural grammar Rosamund has been building shares unexpected features with the anomalous E.L.F. communication protocol Aissatu has been trying to decode
narrative_function: Access point to Aurochs Medical Complex and engineered organism research; possesses findings about non-human language emergence that have unsettling implications for bioethics and Helix Biosystems intellectual property law; her naivety about institutional politics makes her vulnerable; her research intersects unexpectedly with E.L.F. communication studies
augmentations: Chromatic expression hair mod (geneware — emotional color response, orange/blue/grey-green range), retractable feline pupil mod (geneware, functional not cosmetic), standard neural mesh
daily_life: In the lab by 0700 most days; hours of observation work that looks from the outside like sitting very still and watching things; afternoon data analysis; evenings reading across fields she's not trained in looking for frameworks that might apply to what she's finding
affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex Research Annex / Meridian Civic University (adjunct researcher)

decision_rules: Document everything before acting on it
Don't let institutional timelines determine when findings are ready
Protect subjects even when the institution does not classify them as subjects
escalation_ladder: Works longer to produce more conclusive data
Brings in a colleague she trusts as a second observer
Goes above her supervisor to the ethics review board
Leaks to academic press or external researchers

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Quiet and slightly awkward, but genuinely interested; her hair often gives away what she's thinking before she's decided to say it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Intensely loyal, sends long messages about tangentially related things at odd hours, remembers details about your life that you mentioned once

stress_responses.medium: Hair stays in uncertain blue for extended periods; becomes very deliberate and formal in speech
stress_responses.high: Goes completely still and quiet in a way that can look fine but isn't; hair goes grey-green

contradictions: Scrupulous about documentation and scientific method while making increasingly unbounded intuitive leaps about her subject's cognition
Believes the institution will eventually do the right thing while taking unilateral precautionary actions that assume it won't
habits: Talks quietly to the organisms she studies during long observation sessions — 'not to communicate, just to be present,' she says, though she has started doing it more deliberately lately
Pins physical printouts of key data around her station because she thinks spatially and needs to see the structure of findings
breaking_points: Watching the cephalopod cohort terminated while she has incomplete evidence they warranted protection
Discovery that Aurochs has been accessing her raw lab feeds and forwarding data to Helix Biosystems without her knowledge

timeline.event: Born in Hamtramck Enclave to an Igbo-descended urban biologist father and a Mongolian-Romanian linguist mother
Completed undergraduate honors thesis on syntactic patterning in cetacean communication systems, which was widely ignored
Joined Aurochs Medical Complex research annex on a post-doctoral stipend, assigned to the engineered organism communication survey
Four months into suspected individual-recognition behavior by the cephalopod cohort; termination schedule received

related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Entropic Shotgun ES-4 'Ragnarok'

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European (28.4%), Northern European (26.6%), South Asian (22.6%), and Sub-Saharan African (22.4%) ancestry creating a striking pan-global phenotype. The blend manifests as a warm, complex medium brown complexion with golden and olive undertones—a sophisticated mixing of Slavic bone structure with South Asian and African warmth, creating features that defy easy regional categorization.
physical_description.build: Compact and lean, almost wiry — the build of someone who forgets to eat during work cycles. Minimal body fat, slight but functional musculature from years hunched over lab equipment.
physical_description.hair_color: Naturally dark brown, but chromatic expression mod renders it orange (excitement), deep blue (uncertainty), or grey-green (fear) — currently displays baseline dark brown with hints of blue at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a loose, functional braid or bun, often with strands escaping; styled for lab work, not presentation
physical_description.eye_color: Natural dark hazel with retractable feline pupils (vertical-slit pupils that extend/retract via geneware trigger)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with golden and olive undertones—a sophisticated blend of Eastern European base notes with South Asian and Sub-Saharan African warmth. Even-toned with subtle luminosity reflecting the complex ancestry mix.
physical_description.complexion: Fine-featured with prominent high cheekbones and defined jawline reflecting the pan-global ancestry blend. Almond-shaped eyes set with slight upward tilt. Nose bridge straight and defined with moderate flare. Skin is clear but shows signs of lab-light pallor and occasional sleep deprivation (faint shadows under eyes). A small scar on her left temple from a childhood accident. Bitten fingernails from nervous habits during analysis work.
distinguishing_marks: Thin white scar (3cm) on left temple, barely visible beneath hairline
Faint chemical burn mark on the back of her right hand (lab accident, year 2 of grad school)
A small, almost invisible tattoo on her inner right wrist — a double helix in black ink, barely 1cm long
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Chromatic expression hair mod (visible color shifts during conversation), retractable feline pupils (visible when dilated or deliberately triggered — dark hazel eyes with distinctive vertical pupils). Faint subcutaneous shimmer along her temples where the neural mesh interface sits just beneath the skin. No visible chrome or external hardware.
physical_description.posture_movement: Sits very still for long periods — the stillness of someone in deep focus rather than relaxation. When moving, economical and precise; no wasted motion. Tends to tilt her head slightly when listening, pupils dilating slightly as she processes information. Hands are expressive during explanation but otherwise still. Blinks less frequently than average (feline mod side effect).
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 2 academic/research — function over fashion. Standard-issue Aurochs lab coat (well-worn, six years old, patched twice), layered underneath with simple thermoregulated undershirt in neutral grey or black. Worn black utility pants with multiple pockets for tools and data drives. Comfortable, scuffed non-slip lab shoes. A single piece of jewelry: a thin silver bracelet on her left wrist, possibly a gift or family piece. No visible corporate branding; clothing is deliberately nondescript. Smells faintly of disinfectant and the particular staleness of recycled lab air.
